bug.title: The dreaming selection aggregate refuses a candidate that abstained on any world, so a policy that may abstain can never be selected
bug.symptoms: `./run.sh dream` exits 1 with selection_ungrounded ("the score of world ... in stratum 'train' must be finite, got -inf") whenever any candidate abstains on any train world. The cycle summary's train_mean, holdout_mean and incumbent_holdout_mean would be -inf for the same reason.
bug.reproduction_steps: In a tmp store, write replay_score rows for two candidates over a train stratum where one candidate has one row with score -inf (NON_COMMITTING_SCORE) and the rest finite. dreaming.commit_selection over those candidates raises SelectionStoreError naming the -inf world.
bug.expected: - dreaming.commit_selection gains a keyword non_committing, with the same two spellings and the same default (refuse) that dreaming.paired already validates (reuse that validator; do not re-spell the literals). With "flat", _aggregate_candidate reads a row whose score is NON_COMMITTING_SCORE (-inf) as 0.0 before the §7 blend; any other non-finite score (NaN, +inf) is still refused as today. With the default, behaviour is unchanged. - orchestrator/dream.py passes non_committing="flat" to commit_selection, and computes train_mean, holdout_mean and incumbent_holdout_mean with -inf read as 0.0. The summary adds train_commit_rate, holdout_commit_rate and incumbent_holdout_commit_rate (the fraction of worlds in that mean whose score was finite). - The scoring member's aggregate_objective is not changed: it still refuses -inf, and the mapping happens before it is called. - Tests: the reproduction raises under the default and selects under "flat", with the abstaining world counted as 0.0; NaN is still refused under "flat"; a bad spelling of non_committing is refused; the dream CLI over a tmp pool whose incumbent abstains on some worlds exits 0 and the summary carries the commit rates and finite means. The dreaming member suite and the orchestrator tests touched pass.
bug.actual: Root cause: dreaming.select._aggregate_candidate hands raw replay_score values to scoring's aggregate_objective, whose feature-263 law refuses -inf; the pre-registration's flat abstention rule was implemented for the paired statistics (29b2fc7) but never for selection or the cycle summary.
bug.constraints: Only the listed files change Do not edit packages/scoring/ or any stored replay_score row Do not edit packages/orchestrator/src/orchestrator/_sandbox_child.py, packages/contract/**, src/app/** (baked into the gVisor runtime root) Do not edit docs/preregistration/, docs/user-journeys/, deploy/shadow/, packages/router/ or the shadow modules

bug.title: M3 has no incumbent that can both explore a bootstrap world and decide on a financial world
bug.symptoms: incumbent.m2.py abstains on every bootstrap world (it never expands a node), and incumbent.example.py raises TypeError on financial worlds (it subtracts from r2_train, which is None on a failed node) and ranks financial nodes by sign-blind ic_mean squared. Neither can be the M3 incumbent.
bug.reproduction_steps: score_on_world(incumbent.m2.py source, any bootstrap world, round_cap=30) returns a miss on every world of hpo, featsel and symreg. score_on_financial_world over a fixture campaign holding a node whose ic_mean is NULL raises TypeError for incumbent.example.py.
bug.expected: - New deploy/dreaming/incumbent.m3.py, exactly as Addendum 3 describes: - Module-level CONTRACT = "question" and _BETA = 0.5; one function _schedule(beta) returning a fresh dict with commit_z = 0.5 + 3.0 * w, frontier_cap = max(1, round(2.0 + 6.0 * w)) and min_observed = 5, where w = beta / (1.0 + beta). Every threshold select uses comes from _schedule, and each constant is a float or int literal the jitter reviser can move. - select(question): read each revealed node's value as its observation's ic_insample when the observation has that attribute and it is not None, else its r2_train; skip None, NaN and infinities. If at least min_observed nodes have values and the highest-valued node (ties by node id ascending) has a z-score (population standard deviation; a zero deviation never clears) of at least commit_z among them, commit it inline with question.commit(node_id); otherwise call question.abstain(). Then, if any revealed observation has an ic_insample attribute (a financial world, whose tree is fully revealed before the first call), return (); otherwise return up to frontier_cap not-yet-revealed legal_actions of revealed nodes in a stable order, and when nothing is revealed yet, abstain and return the legal roots. - A module docstring stating the rule, citing Addendum 3, and explaining why one commit_z governs both pools. - test_m3_incumbent.py: - policy_runtime.screen_policy admits the module under the strict question-contract rule - on one fixture world per bootstrap domain it explores past the root and commits a node - on a fixture financial campaign it commits the z-top node when it clears, abstains when none does or fewer than min_observed have values, calls select once, and does not raise on a NULL-ic_mean node - the jitter reviser's revisions of it are still admitted Use fixtures only, no sandbox and no real store; the orchestrator tests touched pass.
bug.actual: Root cause: the pre-registration's incumbent (incumbent.m2.py) is a pick-among-evaluated rule that suits pre-evaluated financial trees only; the shipped example explores but was written for bootstrap observations only. No policy reads the two pools' observations through one commit rule.
bug.constraints: Only the two new files are created; no existing file changes Do not edit deploy/dreaming/incumbent.m2.py or deploy/dreaming/incumbent.example.py Do not edit docs/preregistration/, docs/user-journeys/, deploy/shadow/, packages/router/ or the shadow modules
